about.title: Moreno Valley Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Falls rarely announce themselves. One moment you are walking through a grocery aisle off Perris Boulevard or crossing a parking lot near Alessandro Boulevard, and the next you are on the ground wondering what just happened. In Moreno Valley and the rest of Riverside County, those moments play out in stores, apartment complexes, restaurants, and office buildings every week. California law does not make property owners responsible for every fall. What it asks is whether the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to fix it or warn you about it. That question of notice usually decides the case, so the first few days matter. Photograph the spill, the broken step, or the missing handrail. Write down who saw it. Ask, in writing, that surveillance footage be kept. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects you with an independent Moreno Valley premises liability attorney who works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Moreno Valley Fall Victims Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Attorneys Who Understand the Notice Requirement
items.desc: Under California law, you generally have to show the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. The attorneys in our network know how to look for cleaning logs, prior complaints, and inspection records that speak to that question.

items.title: Help Preserving Video Before It Disappears
items.desc: Many Moreno Valley businesses overwrite security footage within days. An attorney can send a preservation demand quickly so the recording of your fall is not lost.

items.question: I fell on a cracked sidewalk maintained by the City of Moreno Valley. Is the deadline different?
items.answer: Yes, and this catches people off guard. While most California premises liability claims carry a two-year deadline, a claim against a public entity such as the City of Moreno Valley or Riverside County must first go through a government claim process with a much shorter window, generally six months from the injury. Because that clock runs quickly, it is worth speaking with an attorney soon after a fall on public property.

items.question: The store says I was not paying attention. Does that end my claim?
items.answer: Not by itself. California follows pure comparative fault, meaning a court can assign a percentage of responsibility to you and still hold the owner accountable for its share. If you were looking at your phone when you slipped on a spill that had been ignored for an hour, your recovery may be reduced, but it is not automatically wiped out.

items.question: What should I do in the days right after a fall at a Moreno Valley business?
items.answer: Get medical care first, even if you think you can walk it off, because fall injuries often worsen over a day or two. Then photograph the hazard and the surrounding area, ask the manager for an incident report, and collect names of anyone who saw what happened. Finally, request in writing that any surveillance video be preserved, since footage is frequently deleted on a short cycle.
